    import React, { createContext, useState, useContext, useEffect, useMemo } from 'react';
    import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage';
    import { api, setAuthFailureListener, resetAuthStatus } from '@/utils/api';
    import { useRootNavigationState, useRouter, useSegments } from 'expo-router';
    
    import { AuthManager } from '@/utils/AuthManager';
    import { getAuthRedirect } from '@/utils/authNavigation';
    
    type AuthContextType = {
      user: (Record<string, any> & { avatar_id?: string | null; avatarId?: string | null }) | null;
      token: string | null;
      isLoading: boolean;
      login: (email: string, password: string, keepSignedIn: boolean) => Promise<{
        success: boolean;
        requirePasswordReset?: boolean;
        userId?: string;
        error?: string;
      }>;
      logout: () => Promise<void>;
      updateAvatar: (avatarId: string) => Promise<void>;
    };
    
    const AuthContext = createContext<AuthContextType | null>(null);
    
    export function useAuth() {
      const context = useContext(AuthContext);
      if (!context) {
        throw new Error('useAuth must be used within an AuthProvider');
      }
      return context;
    }
    
    export function AuthProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
      const [user, setUser] = useState<any>(null);
      const [token, setToken] = useState<string | null>(null);
      const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(true);
      const segments = useSegments();
      const router = useRouter();
      const navigationState = useRootNavigationState();
    
      useEffect(() => {
        const redirect = getAuthRedirect({
          isLoading,
          user,
          firstSegment: segments[0],
          navigationReady: Boolean(navigationState?.key),
        });
        if (redirect) router.replace(redirect);
      }, [user, isLoading, navigationState?.key, router, segments]);
    
      useEffect(() => {
        // Listen for global auth failures (401s)
        setAuthFailureListener(() => {
          console.warn('[AUTH] Global interceptor triggered logout');
          setToken(null);
          setUser(null);
        });
    
        const check = async () => {
          try {
            const shouldRestoreSession = await AuthManager.shouldRestoreSession();
            if (!shouldRestoreSession) {
              await AuthManager.clearSession();
              setToken(null);
              setUser(null);
              return;
            }
    
            const userData = await AuthManager.getUserData();
            const token = await AuthManager.getValidToken();
    
            if (token && userData) {
              resetAuthStatus();
              setToken(token);
              setUser(userData);
            } else {
              await AuthManager.clearSession();
              setToken(null);
              setUser(null);
            }
          } finally {
            setIsLoading(false);
          }
        };
        check();
      }, []);
    
      const login = async (email: string, password: string, keepSignedIn: boolean) => {
        try {
          const res = await api.post('/api/auth/login', { email, password });
          const data = res.data;
    
          // Handle password reset requirement
          if (data.require_password_reset) {
            return {
              success: false,
              requirePasswordReset: true,
              userId: data.id || data.userId
            };
          }
    
          if (data.token && data.refreshToken) {
            await AuthManager.saveSession(data.token, data.refreshToken, data, keepSignedIn);
            resetAuthStatus();
            setToken(data.token);
            setUser(data);
            return { success: true };
          }
          return { success: false, error: 'No token' };
        } catch (err: any) {
          return { success: false, error: err.response?.data?.error || 'Fail' };
        }
      };

    import catalog from './riderAvatarCatalog.json';
    
    const avatarIds = catalog.map((entry) => entry.id);
    
    /** Assigns an existing static avatar consistently without storing it in users. */
    export function getDefaultRiderAvatarId(identity: string): string {
      const key = identity.trim() || 'rider';
      const hash = Array.from(key).reduce((sum, character) => sum + character.charCodeAt(0), 0);
      return avatarIds[hash % avatarIds.length];
    }

    # Systematic Debugging
    
    ## Overview
    
    **Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.
    
    **Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**
    
    ## The Iron Law
    
    ```
    NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
    ```
    
    If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.
    
    ## When to Use
    
    Use for ANY technical issue:
    - Test failures
    - Bugs in production
    - Unexpected behavior
    - Performance problems
    - Build failures
    - Integration issues
    
    **Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
    - Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
    - "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
    - You've already tried multiple fixes
    - Previous fix didn't work
    - You don't fully understand the issue
    
    **Don't skip when:**
    - Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
    - You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
    - Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)
    
    ## The Four Phases
    
    You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
    
    ### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation
    
    **BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**
    
    1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
       - Don't skip past errors or warnings
       - They often contain the exact solution
       - Read stack traces completely
       - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes
    
    2. **Reproduce Consistently**
       - Can you trigger it reliably?
       - What are the exact steps?
       - Does it happen every time?
       - If not reproducible â†’ gather more data, don't guess
    
    3. **Check Recent Changes**
       - What changed that could cause this?
       - Git diff, recent commits
       - New dependencies, config changes
       - Environmental differences
    
    4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**
    
       **WHEN system has multiple components (CI â†’ build â†’ signing, API â†’ service â†’ database):**
    
       **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
       ```
       For EACH component boundary:
         - Log what data enters component
         - Log what data exits component
         - Verify environment/config propagation
         - Check state at each layer
    
       Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
       THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
       THEN investigate that specific component
       ```
    
       **Example (multi-layer system):**
       ```bash
       # Layer 1: Workflow
       echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
       echo "IDENTITY: ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}"
    
       # Layer 2: Build script
       echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
       env | grep IDENTITY || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"
    
       # Layer 3: Signing script
       echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
       security list-keychains
       security find-identity -v
    
       # Layer 4: Actual signing
       codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
       ```
    
       **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets â†’ workflow âœ“, workflow â†’ build âœ—)
    
    5. **Trace Data Flow**
    
       **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**
    
       See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.
    
       **Quick version:**
       - Where does bad value originate?
       - What called this with bad value?
       - Keep tracing up until you find the source
       - Fix at source, not at symptom
    
    ### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

    # Test-Driven Development (TDD)
    
    ## Overview
    
    Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.
    
    **Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.
    
    **Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**
    
    ## When to Use
    
    **Always:**
    - New features
    - Bug fixes
    - Refactoring
    - Behavior changes
    
    **Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
    - Throwaway prototypes
    - Generated code
    - Configuration files
    
    Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.
    
    ## The Iron Law
    
    ```
    NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
    ```
    
    Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.
    
    **No exceptions:**
    - Don't keep it as "reference"
    - Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
    - Don't look at it
    - Delete means delete
    
    Implement fresh from tests. Period.
    
    ## Red-Green-Refactor
    
    ```dot
    digraph tdd_cycle {
        rankdir=LR;
        red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
        verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
        green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
        verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
        refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
        next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];
    
        red -> verify_red;
        verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
        verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
        green -> verify_green;
        verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
        verify_green -> green [label="no"];
        refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
        verify_green -> next;
        next -> red;
    }
    ```
    
    ### RED - Write Failing Test
    
    Write one minimal test showing what should happen.
    
    <Good>
    ```typescript
    test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
      let attempts = 0;
      const operation = () => {
        attempts++;
        if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
        return 'success';
      };
    
      const result = await retryOperation(operation);
    
      expect(result).toBe('success');
      expect(attempts).toBe(3);
    });
    ```
    Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
    </Good>
    
    <Bad>
    ```typescript
    test('retry works', async () => {
      const mock = jest.fn()
        .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
        .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
        .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
    # Writing Good Tests
    
    **Load this reference when:** writing or changing tests, adding mocks, or
    adding cleanup/helper methods for tests.
    
    ## Overview
    
    A test exists to catch a specific break. Two principles govern everything
    here:
    
    ```
    1. Every test names the break it catches
    2. Every test exercises the real thing
    ```
    
    Strict TDD produces both naturally: a test written first and watched
    failing against real code has already proven it can fail, and only earns
    a mock when the real dependency proves slow or external.
    
    ## Principle 1: Name the Break
    
    Before writing the test body, answer: **what production change should
    make this test fail â€” and is that change a bug or a decision?** A test
    earns its place by catching a wrong branch, missing side effect, wrong
    argument, boundary case, or broken contract.
    
    **Derive expectations independently.** Use literals and hand-checked
    fixtures; table-driven tests with literal `want` values are the preferred
    shape. An expectation computed by the code under test â€” or its helpers â€”
    passes no matter what that code does:
    
    ```typescript
    // âŒ Mirror assertion: the same builder computes both sides â€” always true
    const expected = buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' });
    expect(buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' })).toBe(expected);
    
    // âœ… Hand-derived literal
    expect(buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' })).toBe('tag:"urgent"');
    ```
    
    **No change detectors.** If only intentional decisions can fail a test â€”
    a constant's value, exact message wording, private structure â€” it fires
    on redesign and sleeps through bugs. Test the behavior that depends on
    the decision: not `expect(MAX_RETRIES).toBe(5)` but "a failing call is
    retried 5 times and the 6th attempt never happens."
    
    **Behavior, not text.** Asserting that a script, skill, or config
    contains an exact line proves only that the source is the source. Run
    scripts against controlled inputs and assert outputs, side effects, or
    exit codes. Documents that instruct agents are tested by the consuming
    agent's behavior (superpowers:writing-skills); prose for humans earns no
    test at all.
    
    **Your code, not the framework.** Test the contract your code makes at
    its boundaries â€” the route you register, the query you emit, the payload
    you produce. Upstream mechanics are their maintainers' tests to write
    (the classic: asserting your router invokes a registered handler â€” that
    is the framework's test, not yours). When upstream behavior genuinely
    surprised you, write one narrow characterization test naming the
    assumption. The same boundary applies inside your code: constructors,
    getters, constants, and trivial forwarding earn tests only when they
    validate, normalize, default, derive, enforce, or cause side effects â€”
    otherwise assert the first consumer-visible result that depends on them.
    
    ### Gate Function
    
    ```
    BEFORE writing the test body:
      Name the production change that would make this test fail.
    
      Cannot name one            â†’ redesign around an observable behavior
      "The source text changed"  â†’ run the artifact and assert its effects
      Only intentional decisions â†’ change detector; test the behavior
                                   that depends on the decision
    
      Confirm the expected value is derived without the code under test.
      IF it reuses the code's logic or helpers:
        Replace it with a literal or hand-checked fixture
    ```
    
    ## Principle 2: Exercise the Real Thing
    
    **The mock earns no assertions.** A mock assertion passes when the mock
    is present and fails when it is absent â€” it says nothing about the
    component. Assert the real component's behavior; if the mock is what you
    are checking, unmock it or delete the assertion.

    // Standard Security Practice: Socket.io Auth Middleware (The Bouncer)
    io.use((socket: any, next) => {
      const token = socket.handshake.auth.token ||
                    (socket.handshake.headers.cookie ?
                      socket.handshake.headers.cookie.split('; ').find((row: any) => row.startsWith('authToken='))?.split('=')[1]
                      : null);
    
      if (!token) {
        return next(new Error('Authentication error: No token provided'));
      }
    
      try {
        const decoded = jwt.verify(token, getJwtSecret(), { algorithms: ['HS256'] }) as any;
        socket.user = decoded; // Store decoded user for room authorization
        next();
      } catch (err) {
        return next(new Error('Authentication error: Invalid token'));
      }
    });

    # Systematic Debugging
    
    ## Overview
    
    **Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.
    
    **Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**
    
    ## The Iron Law
    
    ```
    NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
    ```
    
    If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.
    
    ## When to Use
    
    Use for ANY technical issue:
    - Test failures
    - Bugs in production
    - Unexpected behavior
    - Performance problems
    - Build failures
    - Integration issues
    
    **Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
    - Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
    - "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
    - You've already tried multiple fixes
    - Previous fix didn't work
    - You don't fully understand the issue
    
    **Don't skip when:**
    - Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
    - You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
    - Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)
    
    ## The Four Phases
    
    You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
    
    ### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation
    
    **BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**
    
    1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
       - Don't skip past errors or warnings
       - They often contain the exact solution
       - Read stack traces completely
       - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes
    
    2. **Reproduce Consistently**
       - Can you trigger it reliably?
       - What are the exact steps?
       - Does it happen every time?
       - If not reproducible â†’ gather more data, don't guess
    
    3. **Check Recent Changes**
       - What changed that could cause this?
       - Git diff, recent commits
       - New dependencies, config changes
       - Environmental differences
    
    4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**
    
       **WHEN system has multiple components (CI â†’ build â†’ signing, API â†’ service â†’ database):**
    
       **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
       ```
       For EACH component boundary:
         - Log what data enters component
         - Log what data exits component
         - Verify environment/config propagation
         - Check state at each layer
    
       Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
       THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
       THEN investigate that specific component
       ```
    
       **Example (multi-layer system):**
       ```bash
       # Layer 1: Workflow
       echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
       echo "IDENTITY: ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}"
    
       # Layer 2: Build script
       echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
       env | grep IDENTITY || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"
    
       # Layer 3: Signing script
       echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
       security list-keychains
       security find-identity -v
    
       # Layer 4: Actual signing
       codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
       ```
    
       **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets â†’ workflow âœ“, workflow â†’ build âœ—)
    
    5. **Trace Data Flow**
    
       **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**
    
       See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.
    
       **Quick version:**
       - Where does bad value originate?
       - What called this with bad value?
       - Keep tracing up until you find the source
       - Fix at source, not at symptom
    
    ### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis
    
    **Find the pattern before fixing:**
    
    1. **Find Working Examples**
       - Locate similar working code in same codebase
       - What works that's similar to what's broken?
    
    2. **Compare Against References**
       - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
       - Don't skim - read every line
       - Understand the pattern fully before applying
    
    3. **Identify Differences**
       - What's different between working and broken?
       - List every difference, however small
       - Don't assume "that can't matter"
    
    4. **Understand Dependencies**
       - What other components does this need?
       - What settings, config, environment?
       - What assumptions does it make?
    
    ### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing
    
    **Scientific method:**
    
    1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
       - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
       - Write it down
       - Be specific, not vague
    
    2. **Test Minimally**
       - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
       - One variable at a time
       - Don't fix multiple things at once
    
    3. **Verify Before Continuing**
       - Did it work? Yes â†’ Phase 4
       - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
       - DON'T add more fixes on top
    
    4. **When You Don't Know**
       - Say "I don't understand X"
       - Don't pretend to know
       - Ask for help
       - Research more
    
    ### Phase 4: Implementation
    
    **Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**
    
    1. **Create Failing Test Case**
       - Simplest possible reproduction
       - Automated test if possible
       - One-off test script if no framework
       - MUST have before fixing
       - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests
    
    2. **Implement Single Fix**
       - Address the root cause identified
       - ONE change at a time
       - No "while I'm here" improvements
       - No bundled refactoring
    
    3. **Verify Fix**
       - Test passes now?
       - No other tests broken?
       - Issue actually resolved?
       - Use the `superpowers:verification-before-completion` skill before claiming success
    
    4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
       - STOP
       - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
       - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
       - **If â‰¥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
       - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion
    
    5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**
    
       **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
       - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
       - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
       - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere
    
       **STOP and question fundamentals:**
       - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
       - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
       - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?
    
       **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**
    
       This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.
    
    ## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process
    
    If you catch yourself thinking:
    - "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
    - "Just try changing X and see if it works"
    - "Add multiple changes, run tests"
    - "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
    - "It's probably X, let me fix that"
    - "I don't fully understand but this might work"
    - "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
    - "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
    - Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
    - **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
    - **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**
    
    **ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**
    
    **If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)
    
    ## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong
    
    **Watch for these redirections:**
    - "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
    - "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
    - "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
    - "Ultra-think this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
    - "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working
    
    **When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.
    
    ## Common Rationalizations
    
    | Excuse | Reality |
    |--------|---------|
    | "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
    | "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
    | "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
    | "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
    | "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
    | "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
    | "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms â‰  understanding root cause. |
    | "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |
    
    ## Quick Reference
    
    | Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
    |-------|---------------|------------------|
    | **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
    | **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
    | **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
    | **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |
    
    ## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"
    
    If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:
    
    1. You've completed the process
    2. Document what you investigated
    3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
    4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation
    
    **But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.
    
    ## Supporting Techniques
    
    These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:
    
    - **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
    - **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
    - **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

    # Test-Driven Development (TDD)
    
    ## Overview
    
    Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.
    
    **Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.
    
    **Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**
    
    ## When to Use
    
    **Always:**
    - New features
    - Bug fixes
    - Refactoring
    - Behavior changes
    
    **Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
    - Throwaway prototypes
    - Generated code
    - Configuration files
    
    Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.
    
    ## The Iron Law
    
    ```
    NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
    ```
    
    Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.
    
    **No exceptions:**
    - Don't keep it as "reference"
    - Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
    - Don't look at it
    - Delete means delete
    
    Implement fresh from tests. Period.
    
    ## Red-Green-Refactor
    
    ```dot
    digraph tdd_cycle {
        rankdir=LR;
        red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
        verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
        green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
        verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
        refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
        next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];
    
        red -> verify_red;
        verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
        verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
        green -> verify_green;
        verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
        verify_green -> green [label="no"];
        refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
        verify_green -> next;
        next -> red;
    }
    ```
    
    ### RED - Write Failing Test
    
    Write one minimal test showing what should happen.
    
    <Good>
    ```typescript
    test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
      let attempts = 0;
      const operation = () => {
        attempts++;
        if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
        return 'success';
      };
    
      const result = await retryOperation(operation);
    
      expect(result).toBe('success');
      expect(attempts).toBe(3);
    });
    ```
    Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
    </Good>
    
    <Bad>
    ```typescript
    test('retry works', async () => {
      const mock = jest.fn()
        .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
        .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
        .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
      await retryOperation(mock);
      expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
    });
    ```
    Vague name, tests mock not code
    </Bad>
    
    **Requirements:**
    - One behavior
    - Clear name
    - Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)
    
    ### Verify RED - Watch It Fail
    
    **MANDATORY. Never skip.**
    
    ```bash
    npm test path/to/test.test.ts
    ```
    
    Confirm:
    - Test fails (not errors)
    - Failure message is expected
    - Fails because feature missing (not typos)
    
    **Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.
    
    **Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.
    
    ### GREEN - Minimal Code
    
    Write simplest code to pass the test.
    
    <Good>
    ```typescript
    async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
      for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        try {
          return await fn();
        } catch (e) {
          if (i === 2) throw e;
        }
      }
      throw new Error('unreachable');
    }
    ```
    Just enough to pass
    </Good>
    
    <Bad>
    ```typescript
    async function retryOperation<T>(
      fn: () => Promise<T>,
      options?: {
        maxRetries?: number;
        backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
        onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
      }
    ): Promise<T> {
      // YAGNI
    }
    ```
    Over-engineered
    </Bad>
    
    Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.
    
    ### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass
    
    **MANDATORY.**
    
    ```bash
    npm test path/to/test.test.ts
    ```
    
    Confirm:
    - Test passes
    - Other tests still pass
    - Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
    
    **Test fails?** Fix code, not test.
    
    **Other tests fail?** Fix now.
    
    **"Other tests" means the project's suite, not just your file.** A
    green run of the test you wrote is not a green suite. Before you call
    the change done, run the project's test command (bare `pytest`,
    `npm test`, `cargo test` â€” whatever the repo uses) even when your task
    named only one test file. A scope statement in your task bounds the
    deliverable, not your verification. Any failure that run shows â€”
    including one you didn't cause â€” goes in your report by name; a red
    test you watched scroll past and didn't mention is a report falsified
    by omission.
    
    ### REFACTOR - Clean Up
    
    After green only:
    - Remove duplication
    - Improve names
    - Extract helpers
    
    Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.
    
    ### Repeat
    
    Next failing test for next feature.
    
    ## Good Tests
    
    | Quality | Good | Bad |
    |---------|------|-----|
    | **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
    | **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
    | **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |
    
    When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
    - Name the production change that would make the test fail â€” before writing it
    - Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
    - Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
    - Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it
    
    ## Common Rationalizations
    
    | Excuse | Reality |
    |--------|---------|
    | "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
    | "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately â€” which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |
    | "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote â€” you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |
    | "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" â‰  comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |
    | "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy â€” that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |
    | "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
    | "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
    | "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
    | "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production â€” slower, not faster. |
    | "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
    | "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |
    
    ## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over
    
    - Code before test
    - Test after implementation
    - Test passes immediately
    - Can't explain why test failed
    - Tests added "later"
    - Rationalizing "just this once"
    - "I already manually tested it"
    - "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
    - "It's about spirit not ritual"
    - "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
    - "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
    - "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
    - "This is different because..."
    
    **All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**
    
    ## Example: Bug Fix
    
    **Bug:** Empty email accepted
    
    **RED**
    ```typescript
    test('rejects empty email', async () => {
      const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
      expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
    });
    ```
    
    **Verify RED**
    ```bash
    $ npm test
    FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
    ```
    
    **GREEN**
    ```typescript
    function submitForm(data: FormData) {
      if (!data.email?.trim()) {
        return { error: 'Email required' };
      }
      // ...
    }
    ```
    
    **Verify GREEN**
    ```bash
    $ npm test
    PASS
    ```
    
    **REFACTOR**
    Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.
    
    ## Verification Checklist
    
    Before marking work complete:
    
    - [ ] Every new function/method has a test
    - [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
    - [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
    - [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
    - [ ] All tests pass
    - [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
    - [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
    - [ ] Edge cases and errors covered
    
    Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.
    
    ## When Stuck
    
    | Problem | Solution |
    |---------|----------|
    | Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
    | Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
    | Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
    | Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |
    
    ## Debugging Integration
    
    Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.
    
    Never fix bugs without a test.
    
    ## Final Rule
    
    ```
    Production code â†’ test exists and failed first
    Otherwise â†’ not TDD
    ```
    
    No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

    # Quality Gate
    
    Run the affected package checks in this order:
    
    1. **Lint** â€” use the package's lint script.
    2. **Typecheck** â€” use the package's typecheck script, or `npx tsc --noEmit` when the package has TypeScript but no script.
    3. **Test** â€” run the package test script, preferably in CI/non-watch mode.
    4. **Build** â€” run the package build script or its documented framework equivalent.
    
    Use the smallest set of affected packages, but include every package touched by the change. In this repository:
    
    - Root web/server: `npm run build` is the available build command. Use the package's existing lint/test commands when present.
    - `mobile-app`: run `npm run lint`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm test -- --runInBand`, then `npx expo export --platform web` unless a more specific release build is required.
    
    Do not install dependencies, change scripts, or weaken checks to make the gate pass without user authorization. Stop at the first failed stage, fix the cause, then rerun the full sequence from lint. If a required command does not exist, report it explicitly and run the closest supported equivalent; never imply that stage passed.
    
    Final reports must name each command, its result, and any pre-existing or unrelated failures. Only call the change complete when all applicable stages have fresh passing evidence.

    import { pool } from '../db';
    
    let ensureTablePromise: Promise<void> | null = null;
    
    export async function ensureRiderAvatarPreferencesTable(): Promise<void> {
      ensureTablePromise ??= pool.query(`
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS rider_avatar_preferences (
          user_id VARCHAR(191) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
          avatar_id VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,
          updated_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
        ) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4
      `).then(() => undefined).catch((error) => {
        ensureTablePromise = null;
        throw error;
      });
      await ensureTablePromise;
    }
    
    export async function saveRiderAvatarPreference(userId: string, avatarId: string): Promise<void> {
      await ensureRiderAvatarPreferencesTable();
      await pool.query(
        'INSERT INTO rider_avatar_preferences (user_id, avatar_id) VALUES (?, ?) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE avatar_id = VALUES(avatar_id)',
        [userId, avatarId],

    import express from 'express';
    import cookieParser from 'cookie-parser';
    import request from 'supertest';
    import jwt from 'jsonwebtoken';
    import argon2 from 'argon2';
    import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
    
    const { query } = vi.hoisted(() => ({ query: vi.fn() }));
    vi.mock('../../db', () => ({ pool: { query } }));
    vi.mock('fs', () => ({ default: { appendFileSync: vi.fn() } }));
    vi.mock('../../presence', () => ({ onlineRiders: new Map() }));
    vi.mock('../../locationTracking', () => ({ handleRiderLocationUpdate: vi.fn() }));
    vi.mock('../../services/connectivityLogger', () => ({ recordConnectivityLog: vi.fn() }));
    vi.mock('../../services/locationEventReceipts', () => ({ ensureLocationEventReceiptsTable: vi.fn() }));
    
    import { authenticate } from '../../middleware/auth';
    import { getJwtSecret } from '../../config/security';
    import usersRouter from '../users';
    import authRouter from '../auth';
    
    const app = express();
    app.use(express.json());
    app.use(cookieParser());
    app.set('io', { to: vi.fn(() => ({ emit: vi.fn() })) });
    app.use('/api/users', authenticate, usersRouter);
    app.use('/api/auth', authRouter);
    
    const tokenFor = (id: string, role: string) => `Bearer ${jwt.sign({ id, role }, getJwtSecret())}`;
    
    describe('rider avatar profile API', () => {
      beforeEach(() => {
        query.mockReset();
        query.mockResolvedValue([{ affectedRows: 1 }, []]);
      });
    
      it('persists the authenticated rider avatar in the preference table', async () => {
        const response = await request(app).patch('/api/users/me/avatar')
          .set('Authorization', tokenFor('rider-1', 'rider'))
          .send({ avatar_id: 'avatar_03', user_id: 'rider-2' });
    
        expect(response.status).toBe(200);
        expect(response.body).toEqual({ avatar_id: 'avatar_03' });
        expect(query).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.stringContaining('INSERT INTO rider_avatar_preferences'), ['rider-1', 'avatar_03']);
      });
    
      it('rejects an unknown avatar ID without writing', async () => {
        const response = await request(app).patch('/api/users/me/avatar')
          .set('Authorization', tokenFor('rider-1', 'rider'))
          .send({ avatar_id: 'https://example.test/photo.png' });
    
        expect(response.status).toBe(400);
        expect(query).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
      });
    
      it('denies a non-rider before writing', async () => {
        const response = await request(app).patch('/api/users/me/avatar')
          .set('Authorization', tokenFor('admin-1', 'admin'))
          .send({ avatar_id: 'avatar_03' });
    
        expect(response.status).toBe(403);
        expect(query).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
      });
    
      it('requires authentication before writing', async () => {
        const response = await request(app).patch('/api/users/me/avatar').send({ avatar_id: 'avatar_03' });
        expect(response.status).toBe(401);
        expect(query).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
      });
    
      it('loads admin and rider lists without requiring a users.avatar_id column', async () => {
        const legacy = { id: 'rider-1', name: 'Riley', email: 'riley@example.test', role: 'rider' };
        query.mockImplementation(async (sql: string) => {
          if (/u\.avatar_id/i.test(sql)) throw new Error("Unknown column 'u.avatar_id' in 'field list'");
          return [[legacy], []];
        });
    
        const all = await request(app).get('/api/users').set('Authorization', tokenFor('admin-1', 'admin'));
        const riders = await request(app).get('/api/users/riders').set('Authorization', tokenFor('admin-1', 'admin'));
    
        expect(all.status).toBe(200);
        expect(riders.status).toBe(200);
        expect(all.body[0]).toMatchObject({ ...legacy, avatar_id: 'avatar_05' });
        expect(riders.body[0]).toMatchObject({ ...legacy, avatar_id: 'avatar_05' });
        expect(query.mock.calls.every(([sql]) => !/u\.avatar_id/i.test(String(sql)))).toBe(true);
      });
    
      it('loads live riders without requiring a users.avatar_id column', async () => {
        query.mockImplementation(async (sql: string) => {
          if (/u\.avatar_id/i.test(sql)) throw new Error("Unknown column 'u.avatar_id' in 'field list'");
          return [[{ id: 'rider-1', name: 'Riley', saved_avatar_id: 'avatar_03' }], []];
        });
        const response = await request(app).get('/api/users/riders/live').set('Authorization', tokenFor('admin-1', 'admin'));
        expect(response.status).toBe(200);
        expect(response.body[0]).toMatchObject({ id: 'rider-1', name: 'Riley', avatar_id: 'avatar_03' });
        expect(query.mock.calls.every(([sql]) => !/u\.avatar_id/i.test(String(sql)))).toBe(true);
      });
    
      it('returns null for a legacy rider login profile', async () => {
        const password_hash = await argon2.hash('1234');
        query.mockImplementation(async (sql: string) => sql.startsWith('SELECT * FROM users WHERE email')
          ? [[{ id: 'rider-1', email: 'riley@example.test', name: 'Riley', role: 'rider', password_hash, avatar_id: null }], []]
          : [{ affectedRows: 1 }, []]);
    
        const response = await request(app).post('/api/auth/login')
          .send({ email: 'riley@example.test', password: '1234' });
    
        expect(response.status).toBe(200);
        expect(response.body).toMatchObject({ id: 'rider-1', name: 'Riley', avatar_id: 'avatar_05' });
        expect(response.body.password_hash).toBeUndefined();
      });
    import { Router, Response } from 'express';
    import { pool } from '../db';
    import crypto from 'crypto';
    import * as argon2 from 'argon2';
    import { onlineRiders } from '../presence';
    import { AuthRequest, authorize } from '../middleware/auth';
    import fs from 'fs';
    import { handleRiderLocationUpdate } from '../locationTracking';
    import { recordConnectivityLog } from '../services/connectivityLogger';
    import { ensureLocationEventReceiptsTable } from '../services/locationEventReceipts';
    import { endShiftSession, getCurrentShiftSession, getShiftSessionsForDate, setNonPresentAttendance, ShiftSessionError, startShiftSession } from '../services/shiftSessions';
    import { getDefaultRiderAvatarId, isRiderAvatarId } from '../services/riderAvatarCatalog';
    import { ensureRiderAvatarPreferencesTable, saveRiderAvatarPreference } from '../services/riderAvatarPreferences';
    
    const router = Router();
    const PH_TODAY_SQL = "DATE(CONVERT_TZ(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), '+00:00', '+08:00'))";
    const PH_NOW_SQL = "CONVERT_TZ(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), '+00:00', '+08:00')";
    
    const getPhilippineDateString = () => {
      const parts = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', {
        timeZone: 'Asia/Manila',
        year: 'numeric',
        month: '2-digit',
        day: '2-digit',
      }).formatToParts(new Date());
      const value = Object.fromEntries(parts.map((part) => [part.type, part.value]));
      return `${value.year}-${value.month}-${value.day}`;
    };
    
    // Get all users (Admin only)
    router.get('/', authorize(['admin']), async (req: AuthRequest, res: Response) => {
      try {
        await ensureRiderAvatarPreferencesTable();
        const [rows]: any = await pool.query("SELECT u.id, u.email, u.name, u.role, u.department, u.status, u.created_at, u.updated_at, u.last_password_change, u.require_password_reset, u.mfa_enabled, rap.avatar_id AS saved_avatar_id FROM users u LEFT JOIN rider_avatar_preferences rap ON rap.user_id = u.id");
        const debugInfo = `[DEBUG ${new Date().toISOString()}] Fetched ${rows.length} users. First row keys: ${Object.keys(rows[0] || {}).join(', ')}\nSample data: ${JSON.stringify(rows[0])}\n`;
        fs.appendFileSync('api_debug.log', debugInfo);
        res.json(rows.map((row: any) => { const { saved_avatar_id, ...user } = row; return { ...user, avatar_id: saved_avatar_id || getDefaultRiderAvatarId(String(row.id)) }; }));
      } catch (error: any) {
        fs.appendFileSync('api_debug.log', `[ERROR] ${error.message}\n`);
        res.status(500).json({ error: 'Database error' });
      }
    });
    
    // Manual MFA reset (Admin only)
    router.post('/:id/reset-mfa', authorize(['admin']), async (req: AuthRequest, res: Response) => {
      try {
        const id = String(req.params.id);
        const [result]: any = await pool.query('UPDATE users SET mfa_secret = NULL, mfa_enabled = FALSE WHERE id = ?', [id]);
        if (result.affectedRows === 0) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'User not found' });
        res.json({ success: true, message: 'MFA reset successfully' });
      } catch (error) {
        res.status(500).json({ error: 'Failed to reset MFA' });
      }
    });
    
    // Get all riders
    router.patch('/me/avatar', authorize(['rider']), async (req: AuthRequest, res: Response) => {
      const avatarId = req.body?.avatar_id;
      if (!isRiderAvatarId(avatarId)) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Invalid avatar ID' });
    
      try {
        await saveRiderAvatarPreference(String(req.user!.id), avatarId);
        req.app.get('io')?.to('admin-room').emit('rider-status-updated', {
          riderId: req.user!.id,
          type: 'avatar',
          avatar_id: avatarId,
        });
        return res.json({ avatar_id: avatarId });
      } catch (error) {
        return res.status(500).json({ error: 'Avatar update failed' });
      }
    });
    
    router.get('/riders', authorize(['admin', 'personnel']), async (req: AuthRequest, res: Response) => {
      try {
        await ensureRiderAvatarPreferencesTable();
        const [rows] = await pool.query("SELECT u.id, u.name, u.email, u.role, rap.avatar_id AS saved_avatar_id FROM users u LEFT JOIN rider_avatar_preferences rap ON rap.user_id = u.id WHERE u.role = 'rider'");
        res.json((rows as any[]).map((row) => { const { saved_avatar_id, ...rider } = row; return { ...rider, avatar_id: saved_avatar_id || getDefaultRiderAvatarId(String(row.id)) }; }));
      } catch (error) {
        res.status(500).json({ error: 'Database error' });
      }
    });
    
    // Get LIVE riders (for Map)
    router.get('/riders/live', authorize(['admin', 'personnel']), async (req: AuthRequest, res: Response) => {
      try {
        await ensureRiderAvatarPreferencesTable();
        // Fetch all riders and their latest info, ensuring unique riders via GROUP BY
        // to prevent duplicate key warnings in the frontend when a rider has multiple active tasks.
        const [rows]: any = await pool.query(`
          SELECT u.id, u.name, u.email, u.status as user_status, u.current_lat, u.current_lng,
                 u.is_on_duty, u.last_battery_level, u.last_signal_strength,
                 rap.avatar_id AS saved_avatar_id,
                 MAX(dr.request_id) as request_id,
                 MAX(dr.delivery_status) as delivery_status,
                 MAX(dr.pickup_address) as pickup_address,
                 MAX(dr.time_window) as time_window,
                 (SELECT status FROM attendance_logs WHERE rider_id = u.id AND date = ${PH_TODAY_SQL} LIMIT 1) as attendance_status
          FROM users u
          LEFT JOIN rider_avatar_preferences rap ON rap.user_id = u.id
          LEFT JOIN delivery_requests dr ON u.id = dr.assigned_rider_id
            AND dr.delivery_status NOT IN ('completed', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'disapproved')
          WHERE u.role = 'rider'
          GROUP BY u.id, u.name, u.email, u.status, u.current_lat, u.current_lng,
                   u.is_on_duty, u.last_battery_level, u.last_signal_strength, rap.avatar_id
        `);
    
        const riders = rows.map((r: any) => ({
          ...r,
          avatar_id: r.saved_avatar_id || getDefaultRiderAvatarId(String(r.id)),
          is_online: onlineRiders.has(r.id),
          last_seen: onlineRiders.get(r.id)?.lastSeen || null
        }));
    
        res.json(riders);
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('[LIVE RIDERS] Route error:', error instanceof Error ? error.message : error);
        res.status(500).json({ error: 'Database error' });
      }
    });

    import { Request, Response, NextFunction } from 'express';
    import jwt from 'jsonwebtoken';
    import { getJwtSecret } from '../config/security';
    
    export interface AuthRequest extends Request {
      user?: {
        id: string;
        email: string;
        name?: string;
        role: string;
        department?: string;
      };
    }
    
    export const authenticate = (req: AuthRequest, res: Response, next: NextFunction) => {
      // Check cookie first, then header
      const token = req.cookies.authToken || (req.headers.authorization?.startsWith('Bearer ') ? req.headers.authorization.split(' ')[1] : null);
    
      if (!token || token === 'null' || token === 'undefined') {
        return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Access denied. No valid token provided.' });
      }
    
      // Handle accidental "rider-session-token" placeholder from old app versions
      if (token === 'rider-session-token') {
        return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Legacy session detected. Please log out and log in again.' });
      }
    
      try {
        // Standard Security Practice: Explicitly enforce HS256 algorithm to prevent protocol confusion attacks
        const decoded = jwt.verify(token, getJwtSecret(), { algorithms: ['HS256'] }) as any;
        req.user = decoded;
        next();
      } catch (error) {
        const msg = (error as Error).message;
        const category = msg === 'jwt expired' ? 'expired' : 'invalid';
        console.warn(`[AUTH] Token verification failed (${category}) on ${req.method} ${req.path}`);
    
        if (msg === 'jwt expired') {
          return res.status(401).json({ error: 'jwt expired', code: 'TOKEN_EXPIRED' });
        }
    
        res.status(401).json({ error: 'Invalid or expired token.' });
      }
    };
    
    export const authorize = (roles: string[]) => {
      return (req: AuthRequest, res: Response, next: NextFunction) => {
        if (!req.user) {
          return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Authentication required' });
        }
    
        if (!roles.includes(req.user.role)) {
          return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Access denied. Insufficient permissions.' });
        }
    
        next();
      };
    };

    import React from 'react';
    import { Card } from '../../ui/card';
    import { User } from 'lucide-react';
    import { cn } from '../../ui/utils';
    import { User as UserType } from '../../../types';
    import { getRiderAvailability, isScheduledForToday } from '../../../utils/riderAvailability';
    import { getDefaultRiderAvatarUrl } from '../../../utils/riderAvatar';
    
    interface RiderType extends UserType {
      attendance_status?: 'present' | 'absent' | 'on_leave' | null;
      is_on_duty?: boolean;
      is_online?: boolean;
    }
    
    interface RiderSelectionListProps {
      riders: RiderType[];
      selectedRiderId: string;
      onSelect: (riderId: string) => void;
      deliveryDate?: string;
    }
    
    export const RiderSelectionList: React.FC<RiderSelectionListProps> = ({
      riders,
      selectedRiderId,
      onSelect,
      deliveryDate,
    }) => {
      const isAssigningForToday = isScheduledForToday(deliveryDate);
      const getAvailability = (rider: RiderType) => getRiderAvailability(rider, isAssigningForToday);
    
    return (
      <div className="space-y-4">
        <div className="flex items-center justify-between">
          <div className="space-y-0.5">
            <h3 className="text-sm font-[900] text-slate-900 tracking-tight flex items-center gap-2">
              <User className="h-4 w-4 text-primary" />
              Assign Rider
            </h3>
            {deliveryDate && (
                <p className="text-[10px] font-bold text-slate-400 uppercase tracking-widest ml-6">
                Schedule for {new Date(`${deliveryDate}T00:00:00`).toLocaleDateString(undefined, { month: 'short', day: 'numeric', year: 'numeric' })}
                </p>
              )}
          </div>
        </div>
    
          <div className="space-y-3">
            {riders.map((rider) => {
              const isSelected = selectedRiderId === rider.id;
              const availability = getAvailability(rider);
              const unavailReason = availability.blockReason;
              const unavailable = !availability.eligible;
              const selectRider = () => {
                if (unavailable) return;
                onSelect(rider.id);
              };
    
              return (
                <Card
                  key={rider.id}
                  role="button"
                  aria-disabled={unavailable}
                  aria-label={`${rider.name}, ${rider.is_online ? 'online' : 'offline'}${unavailable && unavailReason ? `, unavailable: ${unavailReason.toLowerCase()}` : ''}`}
                  tabIndex={unavailable ? -1 : 0}
                  onClick={selectRider}
                  onKeyDown={(event) => {
                    if (event.key !== 'Enter' && event.key !== ' ') return;
                    event.preventDefault();
                    selectRider();
                  }}
                  className={cn(
                    "p-3 rounded-xl border transition-colors cursor-pointer relative group focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-primary focus-visible:ring-offset-2",
                    isSelected
                      ? "border-primary bg-primary/5 shadow-sm"
                      : (unavailable
                          ? "border-slate-100 bg-slate-50 opacity-60 grayscale cursor-not-allowed"
                          : "border-slate-200 bg-white hover:border-slate-300 hover:bg-slate-50")
                  )}
                >
                  <div className="flex min-h-10 items-center gap-3">
                    <img
                      src={getDefaultRiderAvatarUrl(rider.id)}
                      alt={`${rider.name} avatar`}
                      className="h-9 w-9 shrink-0 rounded-full object-cover"
                      loading="lazy"
                    />
    
                    <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
                      <p className={cn("truncate text-sm font-bold", unavailable ? "text-slate-500" : "text-slate-900")}>
                        {rider.name}
                      </p>
                    </div>
    
                    <span className={cn(
                      "shrink-0 rounded-full px-2 py-1 text-[10px] font-bold uppercase tracking-wide",
                      rider.is_online ? "bg-emerald-50 text-emerald-700" : "bg-slate-100 text-slate-600",
                    )}>
                      {rider.is_online ? 'Online' : 'Offline'}
                    </span>
    
                    <div className={cn(
                      "flex h-5 w-5 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-full border-2 transition-colors",
                      isSelected ? "border-primary bg-primary" : "border-slate-300 bg-white",
                    )} aria-hidden="true">
                      {isSelected && <div className="h-2 w-2 rounded-full bg-white" />}
                    </div>
                  </div>
                </Card>
              );
            })}
          </div>
        </div>
      );
    };

The assignment list also may not refetch on avatar save. I’m correcting those rendering paths and making the assignment list respond to the same real-time update.

    // @vitest-environment jsdom
    import { cleanup, fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
    import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
    import { RiderSelectionList } from '../RiderSelectionList';
    
    const today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
    
    const renderList = (rider: any, deliveryDate = today) => {
      cleanup();
      const onSelect = vi.fn();
      render(
        <RiderSelectionList
          riders={[{ id: 'rider-1', name: 'Rider One', ...rider }] as any}
          selectedRiderId=""
          onSelect={onSelect}
          deliveryDate={deliveryDate}
        />,
      );
      return onSelect;
    };
    
    describe('RiderSelectionList availability', () => {
      it('shows only the rider identity and online status when no attendance report exists', () => {
        const onSelect = renderList({ is_online: true, is_on_duty: true, attendance_status: null });
        expect(screen.queryByText(/NO REPORT/i)).toBeNull();
        expect(screen.queryByText('4.9')).toBeNull();
        expect(screen.queryByText(/km away/i)).toBeNull();
        expect(screen.queryByText(/jobs/i)).toBeNull();
        expect(screen.getByText(/ONLINE/i)).toBeTruthy();
        fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: /Rider One/i }));
        expect(onSelect).toHaveBeenCalledWith('rider-1');
      });
    
      it('shows the existing static avatar image without an avatar field from the API', () => {
        renderList({ is_online: true, is_on_duty: true });
        expect(screen.getByRole('img', { name: 'Rider One avatar' }).getAttribute('src'))
          .toBe('/rider-avatars/avatar_05.png');
      });
    
      it('does not select an absent rider for a same-day task', () => {
        const onSelect = renderList({ is_online: true, is_on_duty: true, attendance_status: 'absent' });
        const card = screen.getByRole('button', { name: /Rider One/i });
        expect(screen.queryByText(/ABSENT/i)).toBeNull();
        expect(screen.getByText(/ONLINE/i)).toBeTruthy();
        fireEvent.click(card);
        fireEvent.keyDown(card, { key: 'Enter' });
        expect(onSelect).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
      });
    
      it('does not block a future task because the rider is absent today', () => {
        const futureDate = new Date(Date.now() + 2 * 86400000).toISOString().slice(0, 10);
        const onSelect = renderList({ is_online: false, is_on_duty: false, attendance_status: 'absent' }, futureDate);
        fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: /Rider One/i }));
        expect(onSelect).toHaveBeenCalledWith('rider-1');
      });
    });

    import catalog from './riderAvatarCatalog.json';
    
    const avatarIds = catalog.map((entry) => entry.id);
    
    /** Assigns an existing static avatar consistently without storing it in users. */
    export function getDefaultRiderAvatarId(identity: string): string {
      const key = identity.trim() || 'rider';
      const hash = Array.from(key).reduce((sum, character) => sum + character.charCodeAt(0), 0);
      return avatarIds[hash % avatarIds.length];
    }

    export function getDistance(lat1: number, lon1: number, lat2: number, lon2: number) {
      const radius = 6371e3;
      const p1 = (lat1 * Math.PI) / 180;
      const p2 = (lat2 * Math.PI) / 180;
      const dP = ((lat2 - lat1) * Math.PI) / 180;
      const dL = ((lon2 - lon1) * Math.PI) / 180;
      const a =
        Math.sin(dP / 2) * Math.sin(dP / 2) +
        Math.cos(p1) * Math.cos(p2) * Math.sin(dL / 2) * Math.sin(dL / 2);
    
      return radius * 2 * Math.atan2(Math.sqrt(a), Math.sqrt(1 - a));
    }
    
    const isPhysicallyPossible = (

      lastCheckpoint?: LocationCheckpoint,
    ) => {
      if (!lastCheckpoint) return true;
    
      const distM = getDistance(lastCheckpoint.lat, lastCheckpoint.lng, newLat, newLng);
      const timeS = (newTimestamp - lastCheckpoint.timestamp) / 1000;
    
      if (timeS <= 0) return true;
    
      const speedKmph = (distM / timeS) * 3.6;

    import crypto from 'crypto';
    
    type Db = { query: (sql: string, values?: any[]) => Promise<any>; getConnection: () => Promise<any> };
    export type ShiftSession = {
      id: string; rider_id: string; start_time: string; end_time: string | null;
      session_state: 'open' | 'closed' | 'legacy_unknown';
      start_operation_id: string | null; end_operation_id: string | null;
      handover_reason: string | null; active_task_count_at_end: number | null;
    };
    export class ShiftSessionError extends Error {
      constructor(public code: 'NO_OPEN_SHIFT' | 'HANDOVER_REQUIRED' | 'OPEN_SHIFT', message: string) { super(message); }
    }
    const NOW = "CONVERT_TZ(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), '+00:00', '+08:00')";
    const TODAY = "DATE(CONVERT_TZ(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), '+00:00', '+08:00'))";
    const activeTaskSql = `SELECT request_id FROM delivery_requests WHERE assigned_rider_id = ? AND delivery_status NOT IN ('completed','failed','cancelled','disapproved') AND (delivery_date <= ${TODAY} OR delivery_status = 'in_progress')`;
    
    export async function startShiftSession(db: Db, input: { riderId: string; operationId: string }) {
      return transition(db, input.riderId, async (conn) => {
        const [replay] = await conn.query(`SELECT ss.* FROM shift_operation_receipts sr JOIN shift_sessions ss ON ss.id=sr.session_id WHERE sr.rider_id=? AND sr.operation_id=? AND sr.operation_kind='start' LIMIT 1`, [input.riderId, input.operationId]);
        if (replay[0]) return replay[0];
        const [opened] = await conn.query("SELECT * FROM shift_sessions WHERE rider_id = ? AND session_state = 'open' ORDER BY start_time DESC LIMIT 1", [input.riderId]);
        if (opened[0]) {
          await recordOperation(conn, input.riderId, input.operationId, 'start', opened[0].id);
          return opened[0];
        }
        const id = `shift_${crypto.randomUUID()}`;
        await conn.query(`INSERT INTO attendance_logs (id,rider_id,date,status,check_in_time) VALUES (?, ?, ${TODAY}, 'present', ${NOW}) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE check_in_time=IF(status='present',check_in_time,${NOW}), status='present'`, [`att_${crypto.randomUUID()}`, input.riderId]);
        await conn.query('UPDATE users SET is_on_duty = TRUE WHERE id = ?', [input.riderId]);
        await conn.query(`INSERT INTO shift_sessions (id,rider_id,start_time,session_state,start_operation_id) VALUES (?, ?, ${NOW}, 'open', ?)`, [id, input.riderId, input.operationId]);
        await conn.query(`INSERT INTO movement_events (id,rider_id,event_type,message,metadata,timestamp) VALUES (?,?,'duty_on','Rider started a shift',NULL,${NOW})`, [`move_${crypto.randomUUID()}`, input.riderId]);
        await recordOperation(conn, input.riderId, input.operationId, 'start', id);
        const [created] = await conn.query('SELECT * FROM shift_sessions WHERE id = ?', [id]);
        return created[0];
      });
    }
    
    export async function endShiftSession(db: Db, input: { riderId: string; operationId: string; reason?: string }) {
      return transition(db, input.riderId, async (conn) => {
        const [replay] = await conn.query(`SELECT ss.* FROM shift_operation_receipts sr JOIN shift_sessions ss ON ss.id=sr.session_id WHERE sr.rider_id=? AND sr.operation_id=? AND sr.operation_kind='end' LIMIT 1`, [input.riderId, input.operationId]);
        if (replay[0]) return replay[0];
        const [open] = await conn.query("SELECT * FROM shift_sessions WHERE rider_id = ? AND session_state = 'open' ORDER BY start_time DESC LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE", [input.riderId]);
        if (!open[0]) throw new ShiftSessionError('NO_OPEN_SHIFT', 'There is no open shift to end.');
        const [tasks] = await conn.query(activeTaskSql, [input.riderId]);
        const reason = input.reason?.trim() || '';
        if (tasks.length && !reason) throw new ShiftSessionError('HANDOVER_REQUIRED', `Cannot go off duty with ${tasks.length} active tasks. Please provide a handover reason.`);
        await conn.query(`UPDATE shift_sessions SET end_time=${NOW}, session_state='closed', end_operation_id=?, handover_reason=?, active_task_count_at_end=? WHERE id=?`, [input.operationId, reason || null, tasks.length, open[0].id]);
        await conn.query('UPDATE users SET is_on_duty = FALSE WHERE id = ?', [input.riderId]);
        await conn.query(`UPDATE attendance_logs SET off_duty_time=${NOW} WHERE rider_id=? AND date=${TODAY}`, [input.riderId]);
        const metadata = tasks.length || reason ? JSON.stringify({ ...(reason ? { handover_reason: reason } : {}), active_task_count: tasks.length }) : null;
        await conn.query(`INSERT INTO movement_events (id,rider_id,event_type,message,metadata,timestamp) VALUES (?,?,'duty_off',?,?,${NOW})`, [`move_${crypto.randomUUID()}`, input.riderId, `Rider toggled duty OFF${tasks.length ? ' (Handover)' : ''}`, metadata]);
        await recordOperation(conn, input.riderId, input.operationId, 'end', open[0].id);
        const [closed] = await conn.query('SELECT * FROM shift_sessions WHERE id = ?', [open[0].id]);
        return closed[0];
      });
    }
    
    export async function setNonPresentAttendance(db: Db, input: { riderId: string; status: 'absent' | 'on_leave'; reason?: string }) {
      return transition(db, input.riderId, async (conn) => {
        const [open] = await conn.query("SELECT id FROM shift_sessions WHERE rider_id = ? AND session_state = 'open' LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE", [input.riderId]);
        if (open[0]) throw new ShiftSessionError('OPEN_SHIFT', 'End your current shift before changing attendance status.');
    
        await conn.query(`INSERT INTO attendance_logs (id, rider_id, date, status, reason, check_in_time)
          VALUES (?, ?, ${TODAY}, ?, ?, ${NOW})
          ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE check_in_time=IF(status <> ?, ${NOW}, check_in_time), reason=?, status=?`,
        [`att_${crypto.randomUUID()}`, input.riderId, input.status, input.reason || null, input.status, input.reason || null, input.status]);
        await conn.query('UPDATE users SET is_on_duty = FALSE WHERE id = ?', [input.riderId]);
        return { status: input.status };
      });
    }
    
    async function recordOperation(conn: any, riderId: string, operationId: string, kind: 'start' | 'end', sessionId: string) {
      await conn.query('INSERT INTO shift_operation_receipts (id,rider_id,operation_id,operation_kind,session_id) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)', [`shift_op_${crypto.randomUUID()}`, riderId, operationId, kind, sessionId]);
    }
    
    async function transition<T>(db: Db, riderId: string, action: (conn: any) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
      const conn = await db.getConnection();
      try {
        await conn.beginTransaction();
        const [riders] = await conn.query('SELECT id FROM users WHERE id = ? FOR UPDATE', [riderId]);
        if (!riders[0]) throw new Error('Rider not found');
        const result = await action(conn);
        await conn.commit();
        return result;
      } catch (error) {
        await conn.rollback();
        throw error;
      } finally { conn.release(); }
    }
    
    export async function getCurrentShiftSession(db: Db, riderId: string) {
      const [rows] = await db.query("SELECT * FROM shift_sessions WHERE rider_id = ? AND session_state = 'open' ORDER BY start_time DESC LIMIT 1", [riderId]);
      return rows[0] || null;
    }
    
    export async function getShiftSessionsForDate(db: Db, riderId: string, date: string) {
      const [rows] = await db.query(`SELECT *, CASE WHEN session_state = 'closed' AND end_time IS NOT NULL THEN TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE,start_time,end_time) ELSE NULL END AS duration_minutes FROM shift_sessions WHERE rider_id=? AND DATE(start_time)=? ORDER BY start_time ASC`, [riderId, date]);
      const totalWorkedMinutes = rows.reduce((sum: number, row: any) => sum + (row.session_state === 'closed' && row.end_time ? Number(row.duration_minutes || 0) : 0), 0);
      return { sessions: rows, total_worked_minutes: totalWorkedMinutes };
    }

        .filter((row) => row.check_in_time)
        .map((row) => ({
          id: `legacy_${row.id}`,
          rider_id: row.rider_id,
          source_attendance_id: row.id,
          start_time: row.check_in_time,
          end_time: row.off_duty_time || null,
          session_state: row.off_duty_time ? 'closed' : row.date === today && Boolean(row.is_on_duty) ? 'open' : 'legacy_unknown',
        }));
    }
    
    function getPhilippineDateString() {
      return new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', { timeZone: 'Asia/Manila', year: 'numeric', month: '2-digit', day: '2-digit' }).format(new Date());
    }
    
    async function migrate(pool, { dryRun = false, logger = console } = {}) {
      const [legacyRows] = await pool.query(
        `SELECT al.id, al.rider_id, DATE_FORMAT(al.date, '%Y-%m-%d') AS date, al.check_in_time, al.off_duty_time, u.is_on_duty
         FROM attendance_logs al LEFT JOIN users u ON u.id = al.rider_id
         WHERE al.check_in_time IS NOT NULL ORDER BY al.id`
      );
      const proposed = buildLegacyShiftSessionRows(legacyRows, getPhilippineDateString());
      const [tableRows] = await pool.query(
        "SELECT COUNT(*) AS table_exists FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = DATABASE() AND table_name = 'shift_sessions'"
      );
      const tableExists = Number(tableRows[0]?.table_exists || 0) > 0;
      let existingSources = new Set();
      if (tableExists) {
        const [sourceRows] = await pool.query('SELECT source_attendance_id FROM shift_sessions WHERE source_attendance_id IS NOT NULL');
        existingSources = new Set(sourceRows.map((row) => row.source_attendance_id));
      }
      const alreadyBackfilled = proposed.filter((row) => existingSources.has(row.source_attendance_id)).length;
      const missing = proposed.length - alreadyBackfilled;
      const classifications = proposed.reduce((counts, row) => ({ ...counts, [row.session_state]: counts[row.session_state] + 1 }), { open: 0, closed: 0, legacy_unknown: 0 });
      if (dryRun) {
        logger.log(`Dry run: ${proposed.length} proposed (${classifications.open} open, ${classifications.closed} closed, ${classifications.legacy_unknown} end unknown); ${alreadyBackfilled} already backfilled; ${missing} would be inserted.`);
        return { proposed: proposed.length, alreadyBackfilled, wouldInsert: missing, ...classifications, dryRun: true };
      }
    
      await pool.query(`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS shift_sessions (
        id VARCHAR(80) PRIMARY KEY,
        rider_id VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
        start_time DATETIME NOT NULL,
        end_time DATETIME NULL,
        session_state ENUM('open','closed','legacy_unknown') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',
        start_operation_id VARCHAR(100) NULL,
        end_operation_id VARCHAR(100) NULL,
        handover_reason VARCHAR(500) NULL,
        active_task_count_at_end INT NULL,
        source_attendance_id VARCHAR(50) NULL,
        created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        updated_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        UNIQUE KEY uq_shift_legacy_attendance (source_attendance_id),
        UNIQUE KEY uq_shift_start_operation (rider_id, start_operation_id),
        UNIQUE KEY uq_shift_end_operation (rider_id, end_operation_id),
        KEY idx_shift_rider_start (rider_id, start_time),
        KEY idx_shift_rider_end (rider_id, end_time)
      ) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci`);
    
      const [stateColumns] = await pool.query("SHOW COLUMNS FROM shift_sessions LIKE 'session_state'");
      if (!stateColumns.length) {
        await pool.query("ALTER TABLE shift_sessions ADD COLUMN session_state ENUM('open','closed','legacy_unknown') NULL AFTER end_time");
      }
      await pool.query(`UPDATE shift_sessions ss
        LEFT JOIN users u ON u.id = ss.rider_id
        SET ss.session_state = CASE
          WHEN ss.end_time IS NOT NULL THEN 'closed'
          WHEN ss.source_attendance_id IS NOT NULL AND DATE(ss.start_time) = ${"DATE(CONVERT_TZ(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), '+00:00', '+08:00'))"} AND COALESCE(u.is_on_duty, 0) = 1 THEN 'open'
          WHEN ss.source_attendance_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'legacy_unknown'
          ELSE 'open'
        END
        WHERE ss.session_state IS NULL`);
      await pool.query("ALTER TABLE shift_sessions MODIFY session_state ENUM('open','closed','legacy_unknown') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open'");
    
      await pool.query(`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS shift_operation_receipts (
        id VARCHAR(80) PRIMARY KEY,
        rider_id VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
        operation_id VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
        operation_kind ENUM('start','end') NOT NULL,
        session_id VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
        created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
        UNIQUE KEY uq_shift_operation (rider_id, operation_id),
        KEY idx_shift_operation_session (session_id)
      ) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci`);
    
      const values = proposed.map((row) => [row.id, row.rider_id, row.start_time, row.end_time, row.session_state, row.source_attendance_id]);
      let inserted = 0;
      if (values.length) {
        const [result] = await pool.query(
          'INSERT IGNORE INTO shift_sessions (id, rider_id, start_time, end_time, session_state, source_attendance_id) VALUES ?',
          [values]
        );
        inserted = Number(result.affectedRows || 0);
      }
      logger.log(`Shift session migration complete: ${proposed.length} legacy rows considered (${classifications.open} open, ${classifications.closed} closed, ${classifications.legacy_unknown} end unknown); ${inserted} inserted; ${alreadyBackfilled} already present.`);
      return { proposed: proposed.length, inserted, alreadyBackfilled, ...classifications, dryRun: false };
    }
    
    async function run() {
      const envPath = path.join(process.cwd(), 'server', '.env');
      if (fs.existsSync(envPath)) dotenv.config({ path: envPath });
      const pool = mysql.createPool({
        host: process.env.DB_HOST || 'localhost',
        port: parseInt(process.env.DB_PORT || '3306', 10),
        user: process.env.DB_USER || 'root',
        password: process.env.DB_PASSWORD || '',
        database: process.env.DB_NAME || 'rider_scheduling',
        timezone: '+08:00',
        dateStrings: true,
      });
      try {
        await migrate(pool, { dryRun: process.argv.includes('--dry-run') });
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('Shift session migration failed:', error.message);
        process.exitCode = 1;
      } finally {
        await pool.end();
      }
    }
    
    if (require.main === module) run();
    module.exports = { buildLegacyShiftSessionRows, migrate };
          return res.status(status).json({ code: error.code, error: error.message });
        }

    import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage';
    import * as Crypto from 'expo-crypto';
    
    const keyFor = (kind: 'start' | 'end') => `@pending_shift_operation_${kind}`;
    
    export async function getOrCreateShiftOperationId(kind: 'start' | 'end'): Promise<string> {
      const key = keyFor(kind);
      const existing = await AsyncStorage.getItem(key);
      if (existing) return existing;
      const id = Crypto.randomUUID();
      await AsyncStorage.setItem(key, id);
      return id;
    }
    
    export async function clearShiftOperationId(kind: 'start' | 'end'): Promise<void> {
      await AsyncStorage.removeItem(keyFor(kind));
    }
    
    export async function applyCommittedDutyResult(
      kind: 'start' | 'end',
      isOnDuty: boolean,
      applyState: (value: boolean) => void,
    ): Promise<boolean> {
      applyState(isOnDuty);
      try {
        await AsyncStorage.setItem('@is_on_duty', isOnDuty ? 'true' : 'false');
      } catch (error) {
        console.warn('[shiftOperationService] Duty cache write failed after server confirmation:', error);
      }
      try {
        await clearShiftOperationId(kind);
      } catch (error) {
        console.warn('[shiftOperationService] Could not clear completed shift operation ID:', error);
      }
      return isOnDuty;
    }

I traced shift times from the Attendance page to the database. The page reads them from `shift_sessions`, with `attendance_logs` as a fallback.

In the database configured for this workspace, there are **no shift sessions for Oct 8 or Oct 9, 2026**. The newest sessions are from Oct 7, so the page has no start or end times to show for those dates. Of 23 stored sessions, 10 older records are marked `legacy_unknown`; their end times weren’t recorded, so they can’t be recovered from this data.

I also found that the page doesn’t check whether the attendance API request succeeded before interpreting its response. A server error could therefore look like an empty attendance list. I haven’t changed that yet. If you’re seeing this on a different date or rider, tell me which one—the local database dates may differ from the data in your running app.
